item.title: Arthur creator Marc Brown sells Martha’s Vineyard home for $6.4 million after 37 years
item.description: Marc Brown, the creator of Arthur, along with his wife, has sold their beloved Martha's Vineyard estate for a substantial $6.4 million. This historic property, meticulously restored over thirty-seven years, was a sanctuary for Brown's creativity, where he penned half the Arthur books. With this sale, they conclude a significant chapter in their lives and have already acquired a new home in New York's Hudson Valley, ready for restoration.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 1998, Costa Rica spread 12,000 tonnes of orange waste; 16 years later, forest biomass rose 176%
item.description: In 1998, about 12,000 metric tonnes of orange peels and pulp were spread over a degraded pasture in Costa Rica as part of an unusual forest restoration experiment. Sixteen years later, researchers found that the site had developed into a dense forest, with richer soil, greater tree diversity and a 176% increase in aboveground biomass.

item.title: Meet Vick Tan: The Minnesota student who turned a teabag into a low-cost arsenic filter
item.description: In a groundbreaking initiative, a student has engineered a teabag designed to extract arsenic from polluted water. This clever pouch incorporates eggshells and magnetic iron oxide, successfully removing over ninety-eight percent of arsenic during rigorous laboratory assessments. Researchers are also investigating possibilities for its reuse and economical manufacturing. This innovation represents a significant leap towards providing accessible and safe drinking water.

item.title: Cops used electrocution gloves to subdue high school students in Omaha, now the school district and parents are pleading with police to stop
item.description: US Immigration and Customs Enforcement plans to acquire electric-shock gloves for $20 million. These devices were recently used on two Omaha high school students by officers. Omaha's superintendent requested the police stop using the gloves in schools. Bellevue police will continue carrying the controversial devices for student safety. Experts and parents criticize the gloves as abusive and inappropriate for schools.

item.title: Who is Nitro Camden? Twitch streamer turns his life around after being kicked out of home
item.description: Nitro Camden went from averaging one Twitch viewer to becoming one of the platform’s most talked-about small creators after a 15,000-viewer raid from StableRonaldo turned into a family confrontation on camera. After being kicked out, Camden received help from Cinna, Adin Ross and other creators. Doja Cat also publicly urged fans to support him. Days later, Camden reached Partner status on both Twitch and Kick and gained over 250,000 followers.

item.title: What happened between YouTubers MeganPlays and Leah Ashe? Their friendship fallout explained
item.description: The friendship between Roblox YouTubers MeganPlays and Leah Ashe has come to a troubled end after Leah started dating Megan's ex-husband. In a heartfelt recent video, Leah apologized for her actions, acknowledging the feeling of betrayal. Meanwhile, MeganPlays opened up about the emotional fallout from her divorce, expressing the profound struggles she's faced, including losing her home and needing therapy.

item.title: Scottish athlete won her country a medal at the Commonwealth Games, but had to return to her McDonald's job days later
item.description: Scottish judoka Summer Shaw made headlines by winning a bronze medal at the Commonwealth Games, only to head back to her part-time McDonald's job to make ends meet for her sporting endeavors. Her engaging TikTok video on the matter caught widespread interest, highlighting her need for further financial support. Eager for sponsorship, she dreams of fully committing to her judo career.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: UK woman ‘saved’ by cancer trial cycles 186 miles to thank her hospital
item.description: Julie Rose pedaled an impressive 186 miles to The Royal Marsden hospital, fueled by optimism after a successful clinical trial for her rare cancer. Within six months of beginning her new medication, her tumors had shown significant reduction. This inspiring journey not only pays tribute to her medical team but also drives vital funding towards innovative cancer research for improved, personalized treatment options.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: GTA 6 Release: Kai Cenat dodges every alleged leak; vows to 100% game first
item.description: Kai Cenat says he has not watched any GTA 6 leaks because he is “committed to the actual game.” During his August 22 livestream, he also promised to become the first person ever to 100% GTA 6. The streamer previously said he could spend unlimited time playing after launch. With GTA 6 arriving in November 2026, Cenat already has his challenge planned.

item.title: In 1900, JP Morgan bought 117 acres for daughter's wedding; land later went to Acadia National Park
item.description: A stretch of Maine coastline that was once part of a wealthy family’s private summer estate is now open to visitors as part of Acadia National Park. The land was donated in 1949 by Eleanor Morgan Satterlee in memory of her mother, Louisa, after the family property was badly damaged in the 1947 fire.

item.title: HasanAbi vs xQc and Asmongold: Hasanabi calls streamers "worm-like" over Charlie Kirk song
item.description: HasanAbi has fired back at xQc, Asmongold, Destiny and others after they criticized his appearance singing the “We Are Charlie Kirk” song. During an August 23 livestream, Hasan called his critics “worm-like individuals” and “opportunists,” while accusing them of farming outrage and relying on algorithm-driven drama. He also argued that the backlash showed a clear double standard around political jokes and criticism.
